![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14217745/assets/8ce8a8061ec087c39ce93d73d0566832f33c4e6ce5c2f5185170c9372a0d88fa.png)

Consider the finite region above bounded by $y=2x+2$ and $y=\sqrt{4x+4},$ as shown above. Calculate the volume of the solid generated when this region is rotated $2\pi $ radians about the $x\text{-axis.}$
question.worked_solution:
Let $f(x)=2x+2$ and $g(x)=\sqrt{4x+4}.$

First, we determine the limits of integration. To do that, we find the intersections of the curves by solving the following equation for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =g(x) \\ 2x+2 & =\sqrt{4x+4} \\ 2(x+1) & =\sqrt{4x+4} \\ 4(x+1)^{2} & =4x+4 \\ {x}^{2}+2x+1 & =x+1 \\ {x}^{2}+x & =0 \\ x(x+1) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the limits of integration are from $x=-1$ to $x=0.$

Let's draw our vertical arrow through the region to determine the inner function and the outer function. The arrow should be pointing *away* from the axis of rotation.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14217745/assets/0a6bdcc071500ac8dd40143c3219a14c80fc73d543d7307cb2c880a22db793a3.png)

The vertical arrow 

- *enters* the region through the inner function $y=f(x)=2x+2,$ and

- *leaves* through the outer function $y=g(x)=\sqrt{4x+4}.$

Therefore, the integral that gives our volume is

$$
\begin{aligned}V & =\pi {\int }_{a}^{b}([\text{outer}]^{2}-[\text{inner}]^{2})\text{d}x \\  & =\pi {\int }_{-1}^{0}({[\sqrt{4x+4}]}^{2}-{[2x+2]}^{2})\text{d}x \\  & =\pi {\int }_{-1}^{0}[4x+4-(2(x+1))^{2}]\text{d}x \\  & =\pi {\int }_{-1}^{0}[4(x+1)-4({x}^{2}+2x+1)]\text{d}x \\  & =4\pi {\int }_{-1}^{0}[x+1-({x}^{2}+2x+1)]\text{d}x \\  & =4\pi {\int }_{-1}^{0}(-{x}^{2}-x)\text{d}x \\  & =4\pi {(-\frac{1}{3}{x}^{3}-\frac{1}{2}{x}^{2})|}_{-1}^{0} \\  & =4\pi (0-(\frac{1}{3}-\frac{1}{2})) \\  & =4\pi (\frac{1}{6}) \\  & =\frac{2\pi }{3}\end{aligned}
$$
